stories.headline: Earthquake of magnitude 4 struck China's Xinjiang
stories.title: Earthquake of magnitude 4 struck China's Xinjiang
stories.summary: Beijing , October 19 : A moderate earthquake of magnitude 4.0 on the Richter scale struck China’s Xinjiang region late Sunday night, according to the National Centre for Seismology. The seismic event occurred at 10:55 PM IST on October 18. According to the NCS, the epicentre was located at Latitude 36.683° N and Longitude 77.064° E. The earthquake originated at a depth of 190 kilometres beneath the Earth's surface, classifying it as an intermediate-to-deep focus quake. Due to the significant depth of the epicentre, surface tremors were likely muted across the region. In a post on X, NCS wrote, "EQ of M: 4.0, On: 18/10/2026 22:55:26 IST, Lat: 36.683 N, Long: 77.064 E, Depth: 190 Km, Location: Xinjiang." No immediate reports of casualties or major structural damage have been received. Local emergency management agencies are monitoring the situation. Earlier in July, an earthquake of magnitude 4.1 struck China on Saturday, according to the National Centre for Seismology (NCS). As per the NCS, the shallow earthquake occurred at a depth of 10 kilometres in the afternoon on July 4th. "EQ of M: 4.1, On: 04/07/2026 15:59:19 IST, Lat: 26.550 N, Long: 98.783 E, Depth: 10 km, Location: China," NCS said on X. It occurred near the border with Myanmar. Shallow earthquakes are generally more dangerous than deep earthquakes. This is because the seismic waves from shallow earthquakes have a shorter distance to travel to the surface, resulting in stronger ground shaking and potentially more damage to structures and greater casualties. China's geographical position makes it highly prone to frequent seismic activity. It is located between the two largest seismic belts, the circum-Pacific seismic belt and the circum-Indian seismic belt. Squeezed by the Pacific plate, the Indian plate and the Philippine plate, the seismic fracture zones are well developed in this region. Since the beginning of the 20th century, more than 800 earthquakes of magnitude 6 or greater have occurred in China. Earthquakes have struck almost all provinces, municipalities, and autonomous regions, except for Guizhou, Zhejiang, and Hong Kong. Since 1949, more than 100 destructive earthquakes have occurred across Chinese provinces, municipalities and autonomous regions, 14 of which are in East China. These earthquakes have caused the deaths of more than 2,70,000 people, representing 54 per cent of the total death toll caused by natural disasters in China. The earthquake-stricken districts cover an area of 3,00,000 square kilometres, with more than 7 million rooms destroyed. Experts note that earthquakes and other natural disasters continue to pose major challenges to China even in peaceful times.

stories.headline: YS Jagan Mohan Reddy calls for PM-LoP-CJI panel to appoint Chief Election Commissioner
stories.title: YS Jagan Mohan Reddy calls for PM-LoP-CJI panel to appoint Chief Election Commissioner
reasons: source: event has 4 copies, primary source counted once
corroboration: 3 independent source groups -> high confidence
article_sentences: Following a meeting with the State Election Commissioner, he demanded central paramilitary deployment and CCTV monitoring to ensure free and fair elections, announcing plans to escalate the matter to the Governor.

Guntur: YSR Congress Party (YSRCP) President and former Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister Y.S. Jagan Mohan Reddy advocated for a transparent and non-partisan procedure for appointing the Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) on Sunday, asserting that the convention of governing parties unilaterally selecting the election chief must cease.
He stated that the selection panel ought to comprise the Prime Minister, the Leader of the Opposition, and the Chief Justice of India.
Addressing a press conference, Reddy remarked, "There must be changes in the system.
The practice of ruling parties selecting the Chief Election Commissioner must come to an end.
In the past, we supported the existing system, but we have now withdrawn our support.”
“The Chief Election Commissioner should be selected through a transparent and impartial process involving the Prime Minister, the Leader of the Opposition, and the Chief Justice of India.
The appointment process must follow a proper system.
Only then can democratic institutions function effectively and maintain public confidence,” he added.

Reddy also alleged that YSRCP candidates were being actively obstructed from submitting their nomination papers, demanding the deployment of central paramilitary forces and comprehensive CCTV monitoring throughout the electoral process.

Following a meeting with State Election Commissioner (SEC) Anil Chandra Punetha in Vijayawada, Jagan stated that he informed the election official of local conditions in the state, alleging systemic interference with nomination filings.

Speaking to journalists outside the SEC Office, Reddy explained that he outlined the irregularities to the commissioner and received an assurance that all prospective candidates would be enabled to lodge their nominations.

stories.headline: India-US trade deal close to being final; complex set of factors involved: Marco Rubio
stories.title: India-US trade deal close to being final; complex set of factors involved: Marco Rubio
stories.summary: The foreign policy of the US, of course, takes into account the war between Russia and Ukraine but it is not solely dominated by that, said Marco Rubio.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: India and the US are close to finalising the trade deal but the entire process involves a complex set of factors that are required to be taken into account, said US Secretary of State Marco Rubio ahead of his trip to India.
Rubio, who is in Uzbekistan now, will arrive in India on October 20.
He will meet External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar.
“We're trying to finalise a trade deal with India right now.
We're very close to doing that,” he told reporters on Monday.
He said the US has had to waive sanctions over the past few months because of the impact on global supplies and prices and the impact on other countries.
He said prices are high in the US but are “really, really high in a bunch of other countries”.
“We have to manage all of these things…Every country has a complex set of factors that it has to take into account.
Geography is real.
For some countries, it's very difficult to acquire energy from alternative sources.
That's not an excuse, but all of that has to be balanced when making foreign policy,” he said.

The foreign policy of the US, of course, takes into account the war between Russia and Ukraine but it is not solely dominated by that, it has to take into account a variety of factors including its bilateral relationships with other countries and what they are realistically capable of being able to do in terms of their own energy supplies, said Rubio.

stories.headline: Delhi Cabinet clears plan to create ₹50-cr. corpus for start-ups
stories.title: Delhi Cabinet clears plan to create ₹50-cr. corpus for start-ups
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'cabinet clears' in title weight 44
candidate gate: no category but HIGH+ priority -> allowed
article_sentences: The Delhi government has approved the setting up of the Go-Delhi Foundation, an initiative aimed at promoting startups, innovation and entrepreneurship in the capital.

The foundation will provide young people, researchers and entrepreneurs with integrated support to turn their ideas into practical products and successful enterprises, the Chief Minister’s Office (CMO) said in a statement on Sunday.
It will have an initial budgetary outlay of ₹50 crore.
The Cabinet, chaired by Chief Minister Rekha Gupta, recently approved the foundation and sanctioned funds to help turn ideas into products and bring them to market.
Chief Minister Rekha Gupta said the initiative is an important step towards bringing together Delhi’s existing entrepreneurial capabilities, educational institutions and research facilities.
“Delhi has nearly 21,000 start-ups recognised by the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT).

Through the Go-Delhi Foundation, these resources will be brought together on a common platform, with a focus on developing new enterprises, attracting investment and creating employment opportunities,” she said.
The foundation will help startups and micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) access product engineering, prototyping, laboratory and testing facilities.
It will also offer mentorship and support entrepreneurs at different stages, from product development and testing to certification preparation and market access, Ms. Gupta said.
The foundation will be established as a not-for-profit company under Section 8 of the Companies Act, 2013, and function under the Delhi government’s Department of Industries.
Government departments will be able to bring their real-world challenges to Delhi’s innovators through the foundation, Ms. Gupta said.
Products and technologies developed to address these challenges could be tested through pilot projects, with successful solutions taken forward for adoption.

stories.headline: Pinarayi Vijayan's link emerges in controversial KIIFB land acquisition in Kannur
stories.title: Pinarayi Vijayan's link emerges in controversial KIIFB land acquisition in Kannur
stories.summary: Pinarayi Vijayan faces scrutiny over KIIFB land acquisition in Kannur amid allegations of irregularities, high land prices, delayed compensation and stalled industrial projects in Kerala.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Pinarayi Vijayan faces scrutiny over KIIFB land acquisition in Kannur amid allegations of irregularities, high land prices, delayed compensation and stalled industrial projects in Kerala.

Thiruvananthapuram: Information has now surfaced that former Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan had called for the urgent acquisition of land in Kannur through the Kerala Infrastructure Investment Fund Board (KIIFB), stressing its necessity for industrial development.
Vijayan, when he led (2016-26) Kerala, pressed for the acquisition during a meeting with the KIIFB chief executive officer, maintaining that the land was essential for industrial development.
The disclosure assumes significance amid allegations of serious irregularities in the acquisition and questions over the high prices paid for the land.
Kerala Industrial Infrastructure Development Corporation (KINFRA) reportedly fixed the price at Rs 2.5 crore per acre in Kannur and Rs 1 crore per acre in Palakkad.

This came out last week when the details of the expert committee headed by former Finance Secretary Sudha Pillai flagged serious irregularities in KIIFB’s land acquisitions during the previous LDF government.
The committee raised concerns over purchases at prices reportedly as high as five times the market value.

Despite the substantial outlay and the stated urgency of the industrial projects, no work has begun on the Kannur land so far, raising questions over the justification for the acquisition and the delay in putting the property to use.
The issue has also left hundreds of small landowners in distress.
More than 700 acres in two villages in Kannur were notified for acquisition around eight years ago, but the affected owners were yet to receive compensation.
They say they cannot mortgage the land to secure loans or cultivate it.
Even new drinking water connections to their homes have reportedly become difficult to obtain because of the acquisition notification.

stories.headline: IMD update: Heavy rain outlook for Kerala, South Interior Karnataka retained
stories.title: IMD update: Heavy rain outlook for Kerala, South Interior Karnataka retained
stories.summary: Ann incoming circulation from Gulf of Thailand will be closely watched as it moves westwards towards the Andaman Sea, where it could likely develop into a low-pressure area and intensify
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Isolated heavy rainfall is likely over Kerala and Mahe for six days, South Interior Karnataka for five days, and Coastal Andhra Pradesh, Yanam and Rayalaseema for three days from Monday as the rain belt shifts to Kerala and Karnataka as the week progresses.
Lakshadweep may receive isolated heavy rainfall for three days from Wednesday, followed by another spell over Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal for three days from Thursday.

The most recognisable city names that come under the meteorological subdivision of South Interior Karnataka are Bengaluru, Mysuru, Tumakuru, Mandya, Hassan, Shivamogga, Chikkamagaluru, Chitradurga, Davanagere and Kolar though weather for individual cities may vary from each other.
It was partly cloudy over Bengaluru at 10.30 am with chances of thundershowers less for most part of the day today (Monday).
The outlook for Chennai for today (Monday) is sun and showers, with rain prospects deteriorating untill midnight.

Probability for rain is at a high of 44 per cent at 11 am, which will progressively decline to 23 per cent by 6 pm, before improving with no break-out scenarios, according to an outlook from the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts (ECMWF).
Rain footprint will shift from north and north-east of the city to west and west-southwest before briefly clearing up by 8 pm.

Clouds and precipitation will likely be focused over an area bounded by Pulicat Lake to Chennai and adjoining coast as well as parts of Puducherry and then west-northwest towards Salem, Tiruchirappalli, parts of Dindigul, Madurai and Thoothukudi with parts of Delta districts also seen making some gains during the day.

An IMD assessment in the morning said the current weather pattern is being sustained by an upper-air cyclonic circulation over the south-west Bay of Bengal and adjoining north Tamil Nadu coast, with a trough extending towards the north-west Bay.
As of today (Monday), other cyclonic circulations persist over North Interior Karnataka, the Gulf of Thailand, and south-east Bangladesh and Tripura.
The incoming circulation from the Gulf of Thailand will be closely watched as it moves westwards towards the Andaman Sea, where it could likely develop into a low-pressure area and intensify.
The IMD broadly shares this outlook, pointing to the possibility of a new rain-bearing system emerging over the Bay of Bengal.
